pairs.question: Etenim quae probabilis ratio est obmutescendi, quia nequeas orator esse perfectus, aut in socordiam conpelli, quia desponderis sapientiam?
pairs.answer: Magnae rei, quantulumcumque possederis, fuisse participem, non minima est gloria.
pairs.derivation: Author poses a rhetorical question (what reasonable ground is there for giving up because one cannot reach perfection) and answers it himself in the next sentence at the start of section [12]. Answer ends at the first full stop, before the next sentence 'Quis ergo, inquis, docebit...' which begins a new, separate question. Section marker [12] stripped.

pairs.question: Quis ergo docebit futurum vilicum, si nullus professor est?
pairs.answer: Verumtamen ut universae disciplinae vix aliquem consultum, sic plurimos partium eius invenias magistros, per quos efficere queas perfectum vilicum.
pairs.derivation: Author voices an interlocutor's question; the framing 'inquis' is dropped as speech-tag narration. The reply opens with a non-answering concession ('Et ego intellego, difficillimum esse ab uno velut auctore cuncta rusticationis consequi praecepta.') which merely grants the difficulty rather than naming a teacher, so the answer's start is advanced to the operative 'Verumtamen...' sentence, which actually answers (there are many teachers of the parts of the discipline). Answer ends at the full stop; what follows ('Nam et arator reperiatur...') is elaboration.
